clarity_findings.claim: The worked example precedes the fact that 30% is the actual base rate, reading as an arbitrary illustration rather than the real default.
clarity_findings.problem: The second sentence says 'at a 30 % rate, a dominion that makes 500 credits pays you 150 credits' before the reader has been told 30% is the actual starting value (that fact only appears two sentences later as a bullet: 'The rate starts at 30 %.'). On first read, the 30% in the example looks like a made-up illustrative number, and the reader only realizes it was the real default in retrospect.
clarity_findings.fix: Move or fold the 'The rate starts at 30 %.' fact ahead of the worked example, e.g. state the base rate first, then give the example using that same number, so the example is read as concrete rather than illustrative.

clarity_findings.claim: The screenshot sits right after the negative-output edge case but doesn't visually reinforce it, since the fixture only shows a normal positive dominion income line.
clarity_findings.problem: The bullet list ends on the edge case ('A dominion with negative output lowers your income...'), then the very next element is the {shot:} of a normal, positive dominion income line (Tratia: 9). The juxtaposition briefly suggests the screenshot illustrates the edge case just mentioned, when it actually illustrates the general 'Dominions' line from the opening paragraph.
clarity_findings.fix: Place the screenshot right after the opening paragraph (which it actually illustrates: 'the credit each dominion pays you') and keep the bulleted mechanics, including the negative-output edge case, as the section that follows it.
